topic.topic: Polls, margins of error and sample size

card.title: How many people make a poll?

body.question: About how many people must a poll ask to get a margin of error of roughly 3 percentage points?
body.reveal: About 1,000. A sample of 1,013 gives a margin of about 3.1% at 95% confidence. The margin shrinks with the square root of the sample size, so quadrupling the sample only halves it.

probes.question: True or false: the larger the sample, the smaller the margin of error.
Roughly how much bigger must a poll's sample be to halve its margin of error?

image_brief.show: File:Urne Ballot box république.jpg shows a bronze ballot box

claims.claim: A sample of 1000 gives margin of error about 3.1% at 95% confidence (so about 1,000 for roughly 3 points)
claims.quote: the maximum margin error for a sample size of 1000 is ±3.1% at 95% confidence level

claims.claim: A sample of 1,013 gives about 3.1% at 95%
claims.note: Verified by calculation: 1.96*sqrt(0.25/1013)=0.0308, about 3.1%; page uses n=1013 giving +-3.1%.

claims.claim: Margin shrinks with the square root of sample size, so quadrupling the sample only halves it (probe 2: four times as big)
claims.note: Verified by calculation: MOE ~ 1/sqrt(n); n x4 -> MOE x 1/2.

claims.claim: Larger sample, smaller margin of error (probe 1)
claims.quote: The larger the sample, the smaller the margin of error.
